title: Pylon vs. Help Scout: When B2B teams outgrow email-first support tools
summary: Comparing Pylon versus Help Scout for your support team? See how they differ when it comes to channels, account context, AI features, and room for growth.
body_markdown:
Help Scout is a straightforward, email-first[help desk](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/help-desk-solutions) for customer support. Its shared interface is easy to use and can be enough for small teams managing general inboxes. But friction tends to appear when accounts grow more complex and customers expect real-time conversations across multiple stakeholders. Conversations move into channels like Slack and Teams, and automation is needed to keep workflows streamlined and avoid human errors.


That’s the point when some teams migrate to Pylon, an all-in-one platform built for account-aware[B2B support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/b2b-customer-service-best-practices-strategies) . Let’s compare Pylon versus Help Scout on features and scalability, so you can choose the solution that best fits how your customers communicate.


## 4 reasons support teams move away from Help Scout


Pylon integration's view


Many teams start with Help Scout, but outgrow it over time and move on to new platforms like Pylon. When that happens, it’s often because of Help Scout’s simplicity. This platform is designed to make support emails feel like personal messages from a friend. That design choice can work well for early-stage companies, but it creates structural limits for[scaling teams](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/scaling-customer-support) .


Here are four common reasons B2B companies make the switch from Help Scout to an alternative like Pylon.


### 1. No native omnichannel support


If you support enterprise accounts, your most critical conversations likely happen in shared Teams or[Slack channels](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-use-slack-for-customer-support) . Help Scout’s Slack integration is an add-on built for internal notifications. It alerts you when a new email arrives, but it doesn’t let you conduct in-depth support chats.


This limitation creates friction for enterprise customers who expect real-time collaboration, and it forces them back into email threads. Your team has to manually copy messages into your help desk to maintain clear records, which hurts productivity. An alternative like Pylon can offer built-in Slack and Teams support, avoiding the need for integrations entirely.


### 2. Lack of account-level context


Help Scout organizes support around individual conversations. This limits flexibility if you manage multiple stakeholders per account. When a new ticket comes in, your team often needs to see the account’s[health score](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/b2b-customer-health-score) and full interaction context across all parties.


Without that visibility, support has to operate in a vacuum, disconnected from your[customer success](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-success) and sales teams. Team members can’t easily see if a customer is up for renewal next month, or if an account recently filed three other critical bugs. What you may need is a platform like Pylon that provides account-level views, rather than treating each conversation like a one-time contact.


### 3. Restrictive AI functions


Help Scout’s AI capabilities are fairly modest, and they only support your team members’ manual work. Features like AI drafting and summarizing help you write emails faster, but they don’t handle work autonomously.


This model doesn’t scale well for teams that need[AI agents](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-set-up-ai-agents) to deal with routine tickets and route complex issues to the right people. True AI-powered customer support software should be able to[trigger automated workflows](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-support-automation) and update information without your team’s input.


### 4. Limited scalability and reporting


For small teams that rely entirely on email, Help Scout is a great tool. But once your team and customer base grow, the lack of advanced routing,[SLA management](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/sla-best-practices) , and omnichannel reporting become roadblocks. You’ll need more complex features and granular analytics than Help Scout can offer.


When your[help desk software](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/help-desk-software-examples) doesn’t offer detailed insights natively, support leaders spend their time sorting through data instead of perfecting customer experiences. Teams that rely on[knowledge bases](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/best-free-knowledge-base-software-for-support) to deflect ticket volume could also find that Help Scout lacks the AI indexing needed for useful self-service at scale.


## What to look for when choosing a support platform


If you’re ready to move beyond Help Scout, it’s important to choose a tool that won’t force you to switch again. When you build your list of “must-haves,” focus on long-term scalability and B2B-specific needs.


These key factors should guide your choice:


- **Your support channel strategy.** If customers demand real-time collaboration, you need a tool built for complex messaging across channels.
- **Data architecture.** Find out if each platform groups data by individual email addresses or company-level accounts. This affects whether you can track account health or just ticket volume.
- **AI capabilities.** Agent-assist tools are helpful, but autonomous workflow handling protects your headcount as you scale.
- **Team size.** A platform that feels lightweight for five people could lack the custom routing and SLA controls you need at fifty.
- **Integrations.** Make sure each solution syncs natively with your CRM and engineering tools.
- **Future-proofing.** You’ll want a platform that can handle the channels your customers will expect two years from now, not just the ones they use today.

## FAQ


### How difficult is it to migrate from Help Scout to Pylon?


Migration from Help Scout is quick. Pylon's migrations team backfills your ticket history and knowledge base, and because Slack and Teams are net-new channels, you start there while your email data moves over. Most teams are fully migrated in one to two weeks with minimal disruption.


### Is Pylon a good fit for companies that are just getting started with structured support?


Pylon is built for B2B teams whose customers already work in Slack or Teams, or who manage multiple stakeholders per account. If support is still light and entirely email-based, Help Scout may be the simpler starting point. The signal to move to Pylon is when channels and account complexity start to outpace an email-first inbox, often around Series A to B. That’s why it’s the best customer support for startups.


### How does Pylon's AI compare to Help Scout's AI for scaling support teams?


Help Scout's AI drafts replies and summarizes threads to speed up agents. Pylon's AI goes further: its account-aware agents resolve routine tickets on their own, flag churn signals, and escalate with full account context, so teams handle more volume without adding headcount.
